children: Equity investors are days from a historically favorable stretch of the four-year presidential cycle.

Carson Investment Research, drawing on FactSet data from 1950 through 2025, shows that the midterm year’s fourth quarter and the first two quarters of year three have been the three strongest periods for the S&P 500 (

That window opens October 1. Midterm-year fourth quarters have averaged a 6.6% gain and finished higher 84.2% of the time. The first quarter of year three has been even more consistent, advancing 7.4% on average and rising in 94.7% of observations. Year-three second quarters have added another 5.0%, with a 73.7% win rate.

The contrast with earlier midterm quarters is sharp. Year-two’s second quarter has been the weakest slot of the cycle, averaging a -2.8% decline. That pattern already failed this year, as stocks posted one of the strongest midterm second quarters on record. Even so, the coming three quarters have historically offered the cycle’s best mix of size and consistency.

Seasonality is a guide, not a forecast. Earnings, rates, and policy will still drive the tape. The calendar, however, is rotating into the stretch the data have long identified as the most constructive phase of a president’s term.

title: History’s sweet spot: Midterms and Q4 kick off the cycle’s best run
